key_insight: Grain-boundary segregation in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni delays the start of plastic flow by lowering the early strain rate, with chemistry at the boundaries contributing most of the effect.
engineering_relevance: Tuning grain-boundary composition in nanocrystalline steels could improve resistance to early yielding and delay plastic deformation under load.
method: Hybrid MD/MC simulations on three independent nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni polycrystals
Compared segregated, annealed, and random controls on the same microstructures
Evaluated response under constant stress and fixed strain-rate loading across multiple temperatures
evidence_signal: Under 4.6 GPa at 300 K, segregated polycrystals reached 50% strain about 16% later than random controls, and at fixed strain rate they showed a 6–7% higher peak stress than annealed controls.
watch_item: The reported Cr enrichment depends strongly on the chosen reference region, so segregation metrics should be interpreted carefully when comparing analyses.
paper_title: Grain-boundary segregation delays the onset of plastic flow in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni
